premise.description: Use two independently associated high-precision cooperative results as a cheap classifier: accept matching BF16 bins and exact-replay disagreements.
premise.variant_a: left-associated three-term QK/PV component sums and forward FP64 K64-split merge
premise.variant_b: right-associated three-term QK/PV component sums and forward FP64 K64-split merge
premise.variant_c: left-associated three-term QK/PV component sums and reverse FP64 K64-split merge
premise.reason_for_global_first: the retained global GQA6/K64 primitive has the same three-term component and split-merge arithmetic and already exposes known exact-output errors without reconstructing the removed SWA candidate

commands.association_variants: same command after source-local right-association and reverse-split diagnostic edits; each edit was removed after its output dump

decision.reason: Neither independent association exposes any BF16 disagreement, so both miss every known exact-output error. One exact mismatch also has bit-identical F32 outputs under both component associations. Consensus is not a valid sparse-replay classifier for this arithmetic.
decision.next: Keep exact scalar association. Screen per-K64 probability publication piggybacked on the already-required V-stage barrier so four dimension waves share identical exp/denominator work without introducing the three barriers that rejected the earlier P-cache4 design.
